title: Stopped Spending and Reinstatement on the Mountain Dining Plans
content:
Spending on a plan in the Mountain Dining Plans range is stopped where the card is reported lost or stolen, or where plan fees have stood unpaid beyond the plan's arrears period counted in calendar days from the day the fee was raised. Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used. A stopped plan keeps its balance and its bonus; only the till is closed to it. Spending starts again when the card has been replaced or the arrears settled, against the plan's reinstatement fee where one applies. A transaction made on a card after it was reported lost is not charged to the household where the report reached the collective before the transaction, judged on the collective's own record of when the report was taken.

## The two grounds

| Ground | What it rests on |
| --- | --- |
| The card is reported lost or stolen | the report taken by the collective |
| Plan fees have stood unpaid beyond the plan's arrears period | the date the fee was raised on the plan, as the collective's record of the plan's account holds it, and the plan's arrears period |

## Counting the arrears period

The clock starts on the day the fee was raised, and that day is day zero. Each following calendar day counts as one, weekends and holidays counting exactly as any other day. The boundary day is the day that falls the plan's arrears period after day zero, and the boundary day itself counts: on that day the fee has stood unpaid for the whole of the period, and the ground is made out. Before the boundary day it is not.

**A boundary reading on hypothetical figures.** A plan carries an arrears period of 21 calendar days and a fee is raised on 2027-01-10. Counting that day as day zero, the twenty-first day is 2027-01-31. On 2027-01-30, the twentieth day, the fee has not stood unpaid beyond the plan's arrears period, and the arrears ground is not made out. On 2027-01-31 it is.

## What a stopped plan keeps, and what starts it again

A plan that has been stopped keeps everything on it. The balance stands where it stood and the bonus already earned stands with it; what has closed is the till, so the card is not taken while the plan is stopped.

| What has happened | Whether spending starts again |
| --- | --- |
| the card has been replaced | yes, against the plan's reinstatement fee where the plan carries one |
| the arrears have been settled | yes, against the plan's reinstatement fee where the plan carries one |

## A transaction after a card is reported lost

Where a transaction is made on a card after the card was reported lost, it is not charged to the household provided the report reached the collective before the transaction. Which came first is judged on the collective's own record of when the report was taken, not on the household's account of when it telephoned.
